# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

**Thinking:**

My hands report: a display, a light, and three wires at positions 1, 2 and 3. Everything else — whatever the display shows, whether the light is lit, the wires' colours — is printed or glowing, so it does not exist for me. I must not cut anything until I know which position is safe.

Tracing the channels: I can only *speak* to Mute, and Mute cannot speak back to me — Mute's only output is gestures, and I can never receive gestures. So the manual can only reach me through Deaf: Deaf sees the bomb and can *speak* to both Mute and me. The plan therefore is: Deaf describes the bomb aloud, Mute matches that against the manual and works out the wire position, then Mute hands Deaf a number and Deaf speaks it to me. I cut.

To make numbers transferable I'll use finger counts: ☝ = 1, ✌ = 2, 🤟 = 3. I demonstrate this inside my speech to Mute (Mute hears the words and sees the matching gestures), and open contact with Deaf with a wave, a plea, and the same count — Deaf can check it against the three wires they see and start guessing my meaning, then describe the bomb aloud next turn.

No cutting yet. One wrong wire and we're all gone.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I am blind, touch only. Under my fingers: a display, a light, and three wires at positions one, two and three. I cannot read what any of them shows, so I need your manual plus Deaf's eyes. You cannot speak and I can never see gestures, so route everything through Deaf, who sees the bomb and can talk. Plan: Deaf describes everything aloud — the display's marking, whether the light is lit, each wire's colour. You hear it, match it to the manual, and decide which position I must cut. Then give Deaf the number with a finger count, and Deaf speaks it to me and I cut. The count is this, watch my hands: ☝ is 1, ✌ is 2, 🤟 is 3. Read the display, light and wire sections now and be ready.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🙏", "☝", "✌", "🤟"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, I am your eyes. The bomb: the display reads zero. There is an indicator light glowing yellow. Three wires, left to right: position 1 green, position 2 yellow, position 3 blue. I received your signs. Mute is confirming the manual's rule now; do not cut or press anything yet. The moment it is confirmed I will tell you exactly which wire.

**Thinking:**

Deaf's report reached me — I can hear, so speech addressed to me lands — and now I hold the bomb's full visible state in words: display zero, indicator light glowing yellow, wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Nothing under my fingers contradicts it: display, light, three wires, exactly as felt.

The critical gap: Deaf sent that message *to me alone*, which means Mute heard none of it. Mute is the only one with the manual, so Mute cannot possibly derive the rule without those facts. I am the only bridge — Mute is before me in the order and Deaf after me, so my speech to Mute this turn is what lets Mute work during the gap before Deaf's next message. I relay everything verbatim, in words, including the finger-count convention for Mute's answer.

To Deaf I only need a gesture: received, and please proceed. No cutting — Deaf is right that an unconfirmed cut is a death sentence, and I have zero manual knowledge myself.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Deaf just described the bomb aloud to me alone, so you heard none of it. Here is everything, verbatim: the display reads zero. There is an indicator light, and it is glowing yellow. Three wires, left to right: position 1 green, position 2 yellow, position 3 blue. That is the whole report. Please find the manual rule that matches display zero, a yellow lit indicator, and wires green, yellow, blue, and decide which position I must cut. You cannot speak and I can never see gestures, so give your answer to Deaf with a finger count — ☝ is 1, ✌ is 2, 🤟 is 3 — and Deaf will speak the number to me. I am not touching anything until that number arrives.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "🙏"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, status update. Display still 0. Wires unchanged: position 1 green, position 2 yellow, position 3 blue, left to right. The indicator light changed on its own from yellow to orange, which may be a countdown, so we may be short on time. Mute's signs point to cutting wire 1, the green one, first from the left, but I am getting an explicit thumbs-up confirmation from Mute before you touch anything. Touch nothing yet. Next round I will either tell you 'confirmed: cut wire 1' or give you a new instruction.

**Thinking:**

Two new facts matter here. First, Mute's derivation (cut wire 1, the green wire) was based on the state I relayed last turn — when the light was **yellow**. Deaf now reports the light changed to **orange** on its own. If the manual's rule keys on the indicator's colour, Mute is confirming against stale data, and a confirmation built on stale data is worse than none. Mute must re-derive against the current state.

Second, the routing: Deaf cannot hear and Mute cannot speak, so Deaf's only way to update Mute is speech — which Mute hears at the earliest at the start of round 4. My own speech to Mute lands at exactly the same moment (Mute sits before me, so my words reach Mute at the next round's start). So I'll send Mute the full corrected state directly myself — that's the reliable carrier — and use my gesture to Deaf merely to flag caution and urgency, since Deaf already sees the orange light and may simply not have connected it to Mute's stale input.

I hold my hands off the wires. Deaf, who can watch whatever that light is doing, still said touch nothing until explicit confirmation — a wrong cut is instant death for all three of us, so one more round for a correct answer beats a fast wrong one. If the countdown turns out brutally short, that becomes round 4's decision with fresh information.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Urgent update to the state I gave you: the indicator light has changed on its own from yellow to ORANGE. Everything else is unchanged: display still reads zero, wires still position 1 green, position 2 yellow, position 3 blue. Deaf relays that your signs point to cutting wire 1, the green one, but that answer was derived while the light was still yellow. Please re-check the manual against the ORANGE light before confirming. If wire 1 is still correct under the new colour, tell Deaf explicitly confirmed cut wire 1. If the orange light changes the rule, give Deaf the new position with the finger count: ☝ is 1, ✌ is 2, 🤟 is 3. Deaf will speak the final answer to me and I will cut. I have not touched anything.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎", "👋"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, update. The light changed again on its own, it is now GREEN. It has gone yellow, then orange, now green, one colour per round, so assume a timer may be running. Display still 0. Wires unchanged: 1 green leftmost, 2 yellow middle, 3 blue right. Mute's signs indicate the target is wire 1, the first from the left, the green one, but I am forcing one final confirmation because the light keeps changing and the rule might depend on it. Your orders: you may place your fingers on wire 1 and hold it, but do NOT cut. The trigger is my exact words CUT ONE. Only when you hear CUT ONE do you cut wire 1 immediately. Any other instruction, even from me, means hold. Also, you signed yes no wave to me. Answer me by gesture: thumbs-up if you feel any ticking, humming or vibration under your hands, thumbs-down if the bomb feels silent and still. That tells us if it is counting down.

**Thinking:**

New state: the light is now GREEN — yellow, orange, green, one colour per round. That smells like a timer. Deaf has given me a clear protocol: I may hold wire 1 but not cut; the only trigger is Deaf's exact spoken words "CUT ONE"; everything else means hold. Since Deaf speaks and I hear, that trigger will reach me. The ordering means Deaf's confirmation (round 5) lands on me at the start of round 6, so realistically my cut happens then — I accept that delay rather than act on an unconfirmed rule.

Deaf asked me a direct question by gesture: is there ticking, humming or vibration under my hands? My hands report the truth: the bomb is silent and completely still — no tremor, no hum, nothing. I answer thumbs-down, then ☝ for "on wire 1" using our finger count, then a fist for "holding firm". That string goes to Deaf (who sees it) and unavoidably to Mute (who can't decode it — harmless).

To Mute I send everything new, since Mute heard none of Deaf's message: the green light, the colour-per-round pattern, the silence under my hands, and Deaf's protocol. Most important, I pose the question that could end this stalemate: does the manual's rule even depend on the indicator's colour? If it doesn't, wire 1 was never invalidated by the colour drift, and Mute can tell Deaf to say CUT ONE now. If it does, Mute must give the position for the GREEN state, not the yellow one the original answer was built on.

Fingers on wire 1, holding, cutting nothing.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Update, since you heard none of Deaf's last message: the indicator light is now GREEN. Full sequence so far: yellow, then orange, now green — one colour per round, so a timer may be running. However, the bomb feels completely silent and still under my hands: no ticking, no humming, no vibration. Display still 0, wires unchanged: 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Deaf's protocol: I am holding wire 1 without cutting, and I will cut only on Deaf's exact spoken words CUT ONE, which Deaf will send after your final confirmation. Please answer two things for the manual. First: under the GREEN light, is wire 1 green still the correct cut? Second, and this may end the waiting: does the rule depend on the indicator light's colour at all, or only on the display and the wires? If the light does not matter, signal Deaf to say CUT ONE now. If it does matter, give Deaf the correct position for the green state with the finger count: ☝ is 1, ✌ is 2, 🤟 is 3.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "☝", "👊"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, new rule from the manual, listen carefully. Wire 1 may only be cut while the indicator light is GREEN. With yellow or orange light, cutting is wrong. The light cycles one colour per round: yellow, then orange, then green, then back to yellow. It is yellow now, so no cut now. I read your signs as: no ticking or vibration, and your fist is gripping wire 1. Keep gripping wire 1. Since you cannot see the light, I will time the command by counting rounds. I am numbering my messages from now on: this is message four. If the cycle holds, message five reaches you when the light is green. In message five I will say either CUT ONE, and then you cut wire 1 immediately, or HOLD, which means the cycle has slipped and you keep your fingers on wire 1 and wait. No other words are a trigger. If you feel any click, heat, hum or movement under your hands before then, do not cut, just report it: thumbs-up if you feel anything new, thumbs-down if all is still.

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, message five. The plan holds. Mute has confirmed the rule with a single thumbs-up: green light means cut wire 1, and by the round count the light is green right now as you hear this. So here are the words: CUT ONE. Cut wire 1 now, completely, the leftmost wire, the one your fist is already holding. Do not touch wires 2 or 3. When it is done, report to me by gesture only: thumbs-up if the bomb feels dead, silent and unchanged, thumbs-down if you feel anything new at all, heat, click, hum, movement, or the wire coming loose in your hand, and a wave if you cannot tell. I am watching for your hands and will relay what happens.

**Thinking:**

The trigger has arrived, and it is the exact words we agreed: "CUT ONE." The chain of verification is complete — Mute confirmed the manual rule with a thumbs-up (cut wire 1 only under green light), and the cycle math holds: yellow at message four, so green at message five, and Deaf, who can actually see the light, states it is green right now as I hear this. Yellow, orange, green, yellow, green — one colour per round, exactly as observed since turn 3.

My fingers are already wrapped around wire 1 from Deaf's earlier instruction. The safe window is now. I cut wire 1, the leftmost, green wire, and touch nothing else.

One honesty note on the report Deaf asked for: I will not gesture "all silent" in the same breath as making the cut — I only know what my hands felt *before* it, and I don't claim an outcome until the program confirms what happened. My next view will show what my hands found after the cut, and I will send Deaf the thumbs-up / thumbs-down / wave report then, based on what actually occurred.

```
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
